 Feet Towards The Value Of 30 Feet X 40 Feet Site
 Allotted To The Petitioner At Devanooru Layout 1St
 Phase, Vide Annex-E. And Etc.,

This Petition Coming On For Further Hearing
 This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 -2-
 Wp No. 11964 of 2017
 Order

Petitioner having lost his land in acquisition for the benefit of the Respondent-Development Authority, has been allotted a site admeasuring 30 feet x 40 feet vide Official Memorandum dated 24.11.2015 at the rate of Rs.800/- per Sq.Ft.

He is complaining against the fixation of the said rate as being contrary to law & justice, more particularly, in the context of a judgment of a Coordinate Bench in his earlier W.P.No.49847/2013 disposed off on 7.11.2014.

2. Learned counsel for the Petitioner vehemently argues that what one has to keep in mind is the extent of land lost in acquisition and the compensation payable for that, while fixing the rate of a site normally allotted on compassionate ground.

When the land lost is 21 guntas for which compensation payable is Rs.6,50,000/- in all, it does not make sense in asking the land-loser to pay a huge sum of Rs.9,60,000/-; he further argues that the fixation of site rate should be on some reasonable & just yardstick; the impugned order not reflecting these aspects, contains an error apparent on its face and therefore, is liable to be voided.

3. After service of notice, the Respondent- Development Authority having entered appearance through its' Sr. Panel Counsel has filed the Statement of Objections on 6.3.2023 opposing the Writ Petition; he also makes submission in justification of the impugned fixation of the price and asks this court not to interfere in matters like this, leaving the things to the wisdom of the statutory authorities who possess accumulated expertise.
4.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court is inclined to grant indulgence in the matter as under and for the following reasons:
(i) Petitioner's land admeasuring 21 guntas in Sy.No.87/2 was acquired vide Notification dated 21.4.2004 and the determination of compensation payable for that is on the basis of notified values for the year 2004 and therefore, the rate of the compensatory site that is allotted vide O.M. dated 24.11.2015 i.e., more than ten years after notification, has to be determined on the basis of the market rates that obtained in the year 2004-05 and not 2015-16.

If date subsequent to Notification is taken,
virtually it amounts to not only taking Petitioner's land free of cost but he has to shell out his own money for buying a small piece of land i.e., 30 x 40 sq.ft.
An argument to the contrary cannot be sustained without striking at the root of law, reason & justice.

sentences.text: (ii) Our Constitution ushers in a Welfare State and therefore, the authority cannot have a profit motive whilst fixing the rate of compensatory sites to be allotted to the land-losers in acquisition for public purpose.

Since decades, the farmers are unhappy with the acquisition of their agricultural lands and therefore, there has been a legislative movement that eventually resulted into Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 being enacted.

entities.text:

2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Although, the said Act is not ipso facto govern the acquisition of the kind, still the Parliament's intent cannot be lost sight of, in a country whose "lifeline is agriculture", as observed by the Apex Court in M.C.MEHTA VS. UNION OF INDIA, (2020) 7 SCC 530.

entities.text: M.C.MEHTA VS. UNION OF INDIA, (2020) 7 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(iii) In the earlier round of litigation, i.e., W.P.No.49847/2013, a Coordinate Bench at paragraph 11,
had observed "...It is needless to state that the appellant shall pay the market value of 30 x 40 feet as per the allotment.

Since we have passed this order as a special case considering the background...
the same shall not be treated as a precedent for other cases."

The factors that make the case special is the allotment of the site in question at a concessional rate in the sense the rate that prevailed during the year of issuance of Preliminary Notification which admittedly is 2004.

If rate of the land is determined on the basis of the year of Preliminary Notification, it sounds unjustly illogical that the land loser should pay the allotment price determined on the basis of the market value of the subsequent years, here more than a decade.

(iv) The vehement submission of learned Sr. Panel Counsel appearing for the respondent-Authority that a Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.3011/2013 between Sri.Thimmanayaka vs. Mysore Urban Development Authority, disposed off on 13.1.2015, has observed that "The land owner is entitled for the cost of the site as on the date of the Preliminary Notification based on the allotment rate during the relevant period while allotting sites in favour of other allottees...", the impugned fixing of the rate for the site in question according with the same, cannot be faltered, is difficult to sustain.

entities.text: Thimmanayaka vs. Mysore Urban Development Authority
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Firstly, the Division Bench referred to the normative process of determining the rates for allotment of sites in question.
This would arguably govern the allotments done in the ordinary course.

When Petitioner's case is treated to be a special one specifically stating that the judgment made therein would not be treated as a precedent, the general norm that otherwise would govern others cannot govern the case of Petitioner.
Otherwise, there would be no significance to the factor that Petitioner was treated differently from rest of the lot, for certain reasons.

(v) The vehement contention of learned Panel Counsel that Petitioner's land was notified for acquisition on 21.4.2004, followed by Final Notification dated 3.2.2005 and individual award having been passed on 11.1.2008, the compensation has been deposited on 30.1.2008 and therefore,
the determination of the sital value has to be on the basis of the market rates that obtained as on the date of allotment i.e., 24.11.2014, cannot come to the rescue of the Respondent, because of the checkered history of the case, that admittedly treated the case of Petitioner as a class apart.

As already mentioned above, the person who has lost his bigger portion of land (21 guntas) cannot be asked to pay the price of a small site (30 x 40 sq.ft) in a sum of Rs.9,60,000/- when the very compensation amount for the said land itself is Rs.6,50,000/-.

The site is allotted only in the year 2014, makes no sense for sustaining the determination of higher sital value inasmuch as the site could have been allotted soon after the acquisition and long before 2014.

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, I make the following directions:
[i] this Writ Petition succeeds;
[ii] the demand for a sital value of Rs.9,60,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakh Sixty Thousand)
only, is set at naught; the Respondent-Authority is directed to re-determine the sital value on the basis of market value for the relevant year namely 2004-05, after notice to Petitioner; [iii] on issuance of a demand notice following such re- determination,
the Petitioner shall pay the sital value and on receipt thereof, the Respondent-Authority shall execute & register a Regular Sale Deed within a period of four weeks.
Delay brooked would attract the levy of costs at the rate of Rs.2,000/- per day payable by the erring officials of the Respondent-Authority, personally.
Now, no costs.

Sd/-
